change.title: pr-38446-flat
change.description: Implement recovery key support for user storage providers
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: Nothing marks a federated recovery code as used
findings.body:
For a local credential, using a code removes it: `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.isValid` calls `removeRecoveryAuthnCode()` and `updateStoredCredential` (RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.java:110-111). For a federated user, `UserCredentialManager.isValid` asks the storage validator first, and once that accepts the input the local provider never runs (UserCredentialManager.java:66-79). The authenticator then reads the federated credential here, but it never tells the storage that a code was spent. So whether a code is single-use depends entirely on each storage provider.

The numbering breaks too. The login bean and this method use `getNextRecoveryAuthnCode()`, which always returns `codes.get(0)` (RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.java:36-41). A provider that rebuilds the model from the remaining codes with `createFromValues` renumbers them from 1 (RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.java:65-67). The user is then asked for "code #1" on every login, even after it was used, which does not match the list they printed.

The reference provider in this PR shows the result: it accepts any of the 12 codes and never removes any (BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:340), so one code works forever.

Fix: after the storage validates a code, have the core consume it (for example, a defined update call that takes the used code or the code index). Or document and enforce the contract that the storage must consume the code and keep the original numbering.

findings.title: `removeStoredCredentialById` targets the local store for a federated credential
findings.body: `getCredential` can now return a credential from the user storage, but when all codes are used the code still calls `credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(id)`. That only touches the local store (UserCredentialManager.java:114-117), so the federated credential is left in place and `isConfiguredFor` keeps returning true from the storage. For a federated credential, use `disableCredentialType(RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE)`, as CredentialDeleteHelper.java:64-69 does.

findings.title: Federated path drops the user label and generation time
findings.body: The `UserCredentialModel` passed to the storage only carries the JSON list of raw codes. The `generatedUserLabel` and `generatedAt` that the required action put into `credentialModel` (RecoveryAuthnCodesAction.java:110) are not passed on. The test provider fills in `Time.currentTimeMillis()` and no label, so a federated credential differs from a local one in the account console. Consider passing the label and creation time to the storage too.

findings.title: Hard-coded provider id, looked up even when not used
findings.body: The literal `"keycloak-recovery-authn-codes"` copies `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProviderFactory.PROVIDER_ID` (RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProviderFactory.java:11), which this module cannot import. That makes it a silent break point if the id ever changes. The provider is also resolved even when the storage accepts the credential. Consider moving the lookup into the `else` branch and adding a comment that ties the literal to the factory constant, or using `createCredentialThroughProvider`.

findings.title: Federated recovery-codes credential has no id
findings.body: `createFromValues` never sets an id (RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.java:58-80), and `getCredentials` does not copy `myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()` onto the model. The id is generated at line 195 but then lost. As a result, `CredentialDeleteHelper` cannot match the credential by id (CredentialDeleteHelper.java:64), and the authenticator's `removeStoredCredentialById(getId())` gets null. Set the id from the stored model.

findings.title: Test never checks that a used code cannot be reused
findings.body: `testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin` logs in once with code 0 and stops. The provider it runs against accepts any stored code and never consumes one (BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:340). A second login with the same code would succeed, and the test would not notice. Add a second login that expects the next code number and rejects the reused code. That covers the single-use guarantee recovery codes are supposed to provide.

contracts.action: Required action persists recovery codes via CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential (storage first, local fallback)
contracts.equivalent_path: CredentialHelper OTP creation (updateCredential, then local provider fallback) at CredentialHelper.java:101
contracts.before_after: Before: always local createCredential. After: UserCredentialManager.updateCredential tries the federated updater if it supports the type, then local CredentialInputUpdaters. RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider is not a CredentialInputUpdater, so a local user falls back to createCredential, which deletes the old credential first.
contracts.visible_effect: For federated storage, the label and generation time are lost; only the raw codes are sent.
contracts.failure_mode: JSON serialization failure throws RuntimeException. Storage disabled: updateCredential returns false, so the codes are stored locally.

contracts.action: Authenticator and login bean read the recovery credential via RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential (federated first)
contracts.before_after: The local path removes the used code and updates the stored credential. The federated path does neither, and on all-codes-used it removes the credential by id from the local store only.
contracts.visible_effect: With federated storage, the login page always asks for code #1, and codes may be reusable.
contracts.failure_mode: No credential: credentialModelOpt.get() throws NoSuchElementException in the login bean (unchanged from before).

summary: This PR lets a user storage provider store and check recovery codes. The core does not consume a federated code once it has been used. Nothing tells the storage a code was spent, the login page always asks for code #1, and removal of a fully used credential goes to the local store only. The PR's reference test provider accepts any stored code and never consumes one, and the new test never tries to reuse a code. Smaller points: the federated path drops the user label and generation time, the test provider loses the credential id, and the provider id is hard-coded.
